readerContract.humanQuestion: Are GPT-6 Sol and Luna something I can choose in my ChatGPT account, and do their lower API prices change what I pay?
readerContract.promisedPayoff: Separate ordinary Chat, Work/Codex and API billing so a reader knows what the announcement does and does not establish for her account.

draftArchitecture.plainAnswer: Sol and Luna are separate models in Work and Codex, not ordinary Chat; their published lower figures are developer API prices, not a ChatGPT subscription bill.
causalSequence: OpenAI released Sol and Luna September 22.
The official release places them in Work and Codex and says Chat is separate.
The release notes say available choices depend on plan and workspace settings.
API prices charge developers by tokens, while an account’s ChatGPT plan/workspace controls model choices.
draftArchitecture.workedCase: A reader can use ordinary Chat personally but open Work through an employer; the model list can differ because the surfaces and workspace rules differ.
draftArchitecture.transferCase: For any model announcement, ask which surface changed, who pays through which meter, and whether account settings constrain the choice.
draftArchitecture.usefulAction: Check whether you are in Chat, Work or Codex, then inspect the current model picker and plan/workspace details before treating the announcement as an available upgrade.
draftArchitecture.formatSpecificStructure: The Story; The LAiDIES Read; What This Means for You; The Cocktail Party Explanation; Class Notes; Sources.
draftArchitecture.antiTemplateDecision: No benchmark scoreboard, universal access statement, account instruction, upgrade recommendation or efficiency promise.
